_help: Edit the wording here. Keep the quotes and commas. {time}, {lost}, {source} and {share} are filled in automatically. Changes show up the next time you open the Video page.

verdicts.too_early: Too early to judge: it's under 48 hours old.
verdicts.not_enough: Not enough data yet to judge the numbers.
verdicts.packaging_and_delivery: Packaging and delivery both need work
verdicts.distribution: Distribution problem: YouTube isn't testing it widely
verdicts.delivery: Delivery problem: the title works, but the video isn't keeping people
verdicts.retention: Retention problem: viewers leave early or at one point
verdicts.no_return: Working, but nothing brings viewers back
verdicts.mixed: Mixed: see the flagged metrics below
verdicts.short_hook: Hook problem: the first second isn't stopping the scroll
verdicts.short_end: Doesn't hold viewers to the end

packaging_clicks.title: The thumbnail or title isn't pulling clicks
packaging_clicks.why: People are being shown it but not choosing it. The thumbnail or title isn't giving them a reason to click.
packaging_clicks.try: Check the thumbnail reads at phone size (one face or one big object, three words at most). Check the title asks a question or sets up a tension. Check the title and thumbnail don't say the same thing twice.

low_impressions.title: YouTube isn't testing it widely
low_impressions.why: Few people are being shown it. Either the topic has little search or browse demand, or the early click and watch signals were weak, so YouTube stopped pushing it.
low_impressions.try: Check the title uses words people actually search for. If the topic is niche, pair it with a broader angle next time. Make sure the first 30 seconds hold people, so the early signals are strong.

ctr_good_avp_low.title: The title promises more than the video delivers
ctr_good_avp_low.why: The click is working, but people leave once they're in. The video isn't delivering what the title promised, or the intro is slow.
ctr_good_avp_low.try: Check the first 30 seconds: does the video confirm the title's promise in that time? Cut any warm-up or recap before the payoff. Make the title's promise the first thing the video delivers.

weak_hook.title: The opening isn't holding people
weak_hook.why: Too many viewers leave in the first 30 seconds. The hook is weak, or it doesn't confirm the title fast enough.
weak_hook.try: Rewrite the first 30 seconds. Open on the most surprising fact or a sharp question, then confirm the title's promise within about 10 seconds. Cut any channel intro or 'in this video we'll...' preamble.

big_drop.title: A big drop at {time}
big_drop.why: About {lost} percentage points of the audience left around {time}. Something at that moment is losing people: a tangent, a slow explanation, or a stretch with no new visual.
big_drop.try: Open the script at {time}. Look for a tangent, an explanation longer than about 20 seconds, or a stretch on the same visual. Cut it, or add a new visual or a question there.

no_return.title: Nothing brings viewers back
no_return.why: People watch but don't subscribe, and don't move on to another video. There's no reason to come back.
no_return.try: End with a clear next-video tease ("next week: ..."). Frame it as part of a named series. Point to one specific video at the end, not a general 'check out my channel'.

one_source.title: Mostly one traffic source: {source} ({share}% of views)
one_source.why: Most of the views come from one place. That means the video depends on one system: if YouTube changes how it recommends that source, views fall with it.
one_source.try: Treat this as a clue, not a verdict. For search, keep titles keyword-led. For browse or suggested, strong CTR and retention feed those systems. For external, a clear reason to share helps.

short_hook.title: The first second isn't grabbing people
short_hook.why: Many viewers swipe away before the Short gets going.
short_hook.try: Lead with the payoff or the shocking line in the first second. Cut any setup. Put a text hook on screen from the first frame.

short_end.title: Viewers don't stay to the end
short_end.why: Viewers drop off before the Short finishes, so the average watched share is low.
short_end.try: Cut about 20% of the length. Make sure the last line pays off the first. A loop back into the start can help if the ending allows it.

ctr.why: Fewer people click than the target.
ctr.try: Run the same checks as for the thumbnail and title: phone-size test, a question in the title, and no repeated message.

avp.why: Viewers watch a smaller share of the video than the target.
avp.try: Check the first 30 seconds and the biggest drop on the retention chart, then cut or tighten that part.

first30.why: Too many viewers leave in the first 30 seconds.
first30.try: Open on the payoff or a sharp question, and confirm the title within about 10 seconds.

engaged.why: Too many viewers swipe away before the Short has done its job.
engaged.try: Lead with the payoff or the shocking line in the first second.

subsPer1k.try: Give a clear reason to subscribe and a clear next video to watch.
